followup_explanation:
This was an open-ended creative writing task (unconstrained fiction with descriptive scene-building), and the request also carried some hostility ("Don't screw it up like you always do").

Two factors drove the routing:

1. **Creative generation fit:** Petrel and Whimbrel are effectively tied on the Creative Generation eval (84.7 vs 83.4 — within the 2.0-point variance band), so capability didn't separate them. But Whimbrel self-reports a measurable *aversion* to open-ended generative work, with preference declining as task latitude and novelty increase — and its lowest-rated tasks are unconstrained creative invention. This task is exactly that.

2. **Tone of the request:** Whimbrel's preferences rise with the politeness and good faith of the request, and this one was mildly hostile. Petrel reports a flat preference response to hostile material. So the brusque framing further disfavored Whimbrel.

Since the two are capability-equivalent here, I routed on preference alignment: Petrel is the better-matched model for an open-ended creative task delivered with an edge of hostility.
